page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.E6.Ax.Flex.2-16 is a general-purpose virtual machine deployed on the x86_64 architecture. Hardware resources are driven by an AMD EPYC 9J45 processor operating at a base clock speed of 2.7 GHz. The instance provisions 2 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading enabled at two threads per core, delivering 4 dedicated vCPUs. Compute resources are balanced with 16.0 GB of system memory, establishing a standard 4.0 GB per vCPU ratio typical of general-purpose cloud profiles.

Storage and hardware acceleration options are distinctly bounded. The server does not bundle local disk storage, necessitating the attachment of remote block volumes for persistent filesystem needs. No discrete GPUs or specialized hardware accelerators are present on this shape. For network connectivity, the configuration provides one complimentary public IPv4 address. Because the compute model employs dedicated core slices rather than fractional burstable scheduling, processing execution avoids credit-exhaustion throttling under sustained runtime demands.

The 1:4 compute-to-memory ratio provides a predictable resource profile for standard business software and service tiers. VM.Standard.E6.Ax.Flex.2-16 is technically aligned with workloads such as web application hosting, backend microservices, container orchestration nodes, integration testing pipelines, and light transactional databases that do not demand extensive local IOPS or accelerator hardware.

System memory is sized at 16.0 GB, providing an even 4.0 GB of memory per core. Lacking discrete GPU acceleration, the shape prioritizes balanced CPU and memory allocation to maintain predictable processing without paying for unused specialized hardware. The resource profile is well-matched for web application servers, containerized application environments, background task workers, and small-to-medium database workloads.
